source.title: Phase Transitions in Attention: A Bayesian Theory of Copy Head Emergence
source.authors: Itay Lavie; Kirsten Fischer; A. Lekov; Frederic Van Maele; Z. Ringel; M. Helias

page_placements.theme: Shape of toy ICL transitions depends on parametrisation, initialisation, task and data size

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study directly analyzes and trains attention models on a shift-by-one copying task, and refines the transition claim by finding different emergence profiles for linear and softmax attention. It does not train or analyze full induction heads in a multilayer next-token language model.
record.gate_note: The tested object is the copy or shift-by-one subcircuit, not the complete induction-head circuit. The study varies training-set size P and reports order parameters and loss per token; it does not measure loss by token index or a bump over training steps. Results cited from other work, including prior studies of induction heads, are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study models and trains only the copy (shift-by-one, previous-token) subcircuit in a single-layer, single-head model on a supervised task. It tracks its emergence as a function of training-set size P, not training steps. No induction head is formed or measured: there is no composition, no [A][B]…[A]→[B] behaviour and no token-index ICL. This is a related but different construct, a component of the induction circuit, so its findings go under fits_no_version rather than as tests of V1–V7. The authors frame the work as studying the first layer of an induction head and leave two-layer induction heads to future work.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct; add three points. The transitions are in the amount of training data P, not training time. Linear attention shows a second-order transition to uniform pooling, then a crossover to copying that is explicitly not a second phase transition. Softmax shows a first-order jump with no precursor, which the authors argue makes onset unpredictable. Softmax also has better sample complexity, by O(√(LV)).
record.recipe_differences: The study develops a Bayesian theory and trains single-layer, single-head models on a supervised shift-by-one copy task, rather than measuring unsupervised induction-head formation during language-model training.
record.method_sensitivity: Transition profile depends on attention activation: linear attention has a pooling transition followed by a copy crossover; softmax attention has one abrupt transition. The phase boundaries also vary with P, L, and V.

fits_no_version.finding: In single-layer softmax attention on a supervised shift-by-one task, the copy order parameter âG jumps discontinuously near P≈300. Loss drops sharply at the same point, with no precursor phase (a first-order transition in dataset size). Adam and SGLD agree closely with theory.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The copy/previous-token subcircuit of softmax attention emerges abruptly (first-order) once training-set size crosses a threshold scaling roughly as L ln²(L).

fits_no_version.finding: In linear attention on the same task, a continuous second-order transition first gives uniform pooling (ĉ1 rises near P≈100). A smooth crossover to copy attention follows beyond P≈400, giving two loss plateaus. The authors relate these stages to the unigram→bigram stages of prior work.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Whether copy-subcircuit formation is staged (pooling then copy) or single-step depends on the attention activation: staged for linear attention, single-step for softmax.

fits_no_version.finding: Theory-predicted phase boundaries track experiment across sequence length L and vocabulary size V. The predicted scalings are P*ĉ1 ~ V² and P*ĉG ~ L^{3/2}V^{1/2} for linear attention, and ~L ln²L for softmax.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The data needed for copy-subcircuit emergence scales predictably with sequence length and vocabulary size, and is smaller for softmax than for linear attention.

record.problems: The experiments use a single-layer, single-head model and a supervised synthetic copy task, so they do not establish formation or role of full induction heads in multilayer language models. Results use strong scaling and equivalent-kernel approximations; the authors note that finite-size corrections and structured or natural-language token distributions remain for future work. Adam results filter runs that did not reach the global minimum. Some reported transitions and phase boundaries are presented in figures without numerical values or uncertainty estimates.

untested.parts: No induction head, no composition with a previous-token head, and no [A][B]…[A]→[B] behaviour. Only the shift-by-one copy head is studied in isolation.
No emergence over training steps, no ICL measure (loss by token index), and no coincident loss bump. Transitions are in training-set size P for a copy head.
Not addressed; only single-layer linear and softmax toy models.
Induction-head formation and ICL persistence are not measured. Data dependence (P, L, V) is shown only for copy-subcircuit formation on i.i.d. uniform tokens.
Sub-steps of induction-head formation are not measured. The staged pooling→copy result concerns only the first-layer copy subcircuit, as a function of P.

missing.what: Test loss versus training epochs for Adam at each P. Linear runs split into two loss clusters (local vs global minima), while all softmax runs reach the global minimum. These are the only training-time dynamics in the paper.
missing.versions: none directly; relevant to V2 only if a future row treats copy-head dynamics over training time

record.verdict_notes: An alternative, looser reading would link R1–R12 to V5 and V7 (copy-subcircuit formation as a sub-step of induction-head formation) and R5–R8 to V2. I rejected it because the rows measure a previous-token head, not an induction head, and track dataset size, not training time. The reader's V1 'supports' and V7 'challenges' (softmax) labels are unfounded on these grounds. Adam results filter out runs stuck in local minima (linear case); the authors say the filtering was by loss only.

versions.untested_parts: Tests learning of the shift-by-one copy pattern in a single-layer, single-head model. Does not test composition with a previous-token head or the full [A][B] … [A] → [B] induction circuit.

Tests abruptness and loss changes as training-set size P varies. Does not test timing over training steps, loss falling with token index, or whether an ICL gain and a training-loss bump occur at the same time.
Does not test the share of in-context learning in large transformers attributable to induction heads.
Does not test induction-head prevalence across model families, sizes, or training runs, or in other architectures or modalities.

Tests dependence on training-set size, sequence length, vocabulary size, and attention activation in the supervised synthetic copy task. Does not test natural-language data, unsupervised next-token training, or persistence of ICL.
Does not compare few-shot task learning with copying, or test whether other mechanisms carry few-shot learning.
Tests whether copy-pattern learning is staged in the studied single-layer models. Does not test substeps in full induction-head formation or in large language models.

rows.subject: single-layer, single-head linear attention model (Adam-trained; ensemble results)
rows.stage_stated: trained on the supervised shift-by-one copy task
rows.operation_detail: Trained on uniformly sampled one-hot sequences while varying the number of training sequences P; reported pooling and copy order parameters.

conditions.value: Adam; runs reaching the global loss minimum are retained for the main results
varied; experimental transition described near P ≈ 100, with copy crossover beyond P ≈ 400

rows.measure: Pooling order parameter ĉ1 and copy order parameter ĉG
rows.value: ĉ1 departs from zero at the experimental transition near P ≈ 100; ĉG remains near zero initially, then grows as ĉ1 declines, with the copy crossover beyond P ≈ 400. The theory gives Pĉ1* ≈ 23 and PĉG* ≈ 322 for the illustrated setting.
rows.uncertainty: 10 models per P; ensemble results are reported. Appendix N states results are averaged over the ensemble at fixed P, while main-text Adam results filter runs that did not reach the global minimum. No uncertainty value for these order parameters is stated in the text.
rows.locator: Sections 3.4 and 4; Figures 1 and 3; Appendix N, Table 1
rows.note: The results describe a continuous pooling onset followed by a later copy crossover, rather than one abrupt copy transition. The difference between the theoretical thresholds and the experimental transition descriptions is retained as reported.
rows.check: Measures pooling/copy order parameters of a previous-token (shift-by-one) head versus training-set size P, not induction heads. V1 needs composition and induction behaviour. V2 needs abrupt emergence over training time with an ICL gain. V5/V7 concern induction-head formation. The experimental pooling onset (~P≈100) differs from the theory threshold (Pĉ1*≈23); the row already notes this. Adam results keep only runs that reached the global minimum.

relation.reason: The study explicitly discusses induction heads as motivation and related work, while studying only their copy subcircuit; testing a two-layer induction circuit is future work.

tranche.reason: The supervised shift-by-one task isolates a previous-token copy subcircuit and varies dataset size P. It does not measure induction-head formation, composition, or the specified in-context learning effects.

source_check.notes: Transitions are versus dataset size P, not training time; the later linear-attention crossover is explicitly not a second phase transition. Adam results retain global-minimum runs; all softmax seeds converged.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: supervised shift-by-one copy task in the single-layer linear and softmax models
reader_labels.reason: The trained attention patterns develop a copy component that implements the task's shift-by-one mapping (R1, R2, R5, R6); composition with a previous-token head is not tested.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: softmax attention as training-set size P varies
reader_labels.reason: The copy order parameter jumps near P ≈ 300 and loss per token drops sharply at that boundary (R5–R8). The study does not establish the claimed training-step timing, token-index ICL gain, or training-loss bump.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: linear attention as training-set size P varies
reader_labels.reason: Copy learning is preceded by a pooling transition and then a later crossover, with two loss plateaus/transition regions rather than one abrupt copy transition (R1–R4).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: supervised synthetic copy task; varied P, L, V, and attention activation
reader_labels.reason: The copy pattern and loss change with training-set size, and the reported boundaries vary across sequence-length and vocabulary-size phase diagrams; linear and softmax attention also have different transition profiles (R1–R12).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: The results show a pooling onset followed by a later copy crossover, described as two stages and not as a second phase transition (R1–R4).

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.reason: The reported softmax results show one abrupt transition directly from uniform attention to copy attention, rather than multiple emergence stages (R5–R8).
